The intervention is physical radiation delivery, so 'target engagement' means the radiation was delivered to the intended anatomical site. Given this is a completed trial with reported outcomes, we can assume the radiation was delivered as planned, though no biomarker data confirms cellular DNA damage. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: The proposed mechanism is high-dose focused radiation causing DNA damage and cell death in residual tumor cells. No biomarker data is available to confirm DNA damage or apoptosis markers, so we cannot directly assess pathway modulation. 3. Additionally, 23/39 patients achieved no evidence of disease (59.0%), which represents an even better outcome. The overall success rate combining local control and NED is substantial. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: The trial shows clear response heterogeneity - 59% achieved NED, 33% had local control, while only 7.7% had progression/recurrence. This suggests the intervention works well in the majority of this population (brain metastases post-surgical resection). 5. CONFOUNDERS: This is a single-arm trial with no control group, but the local control rate appears clinically meaningful for this indication. The 52-week follow-up duration is appropriate for assessing local control. Sample size of 51 is reasonable for this type of intervention study.
